comments.author: Poornachandra Kongara
comments.comment:
Most 2027 GenAI roadmaps skip the boring part: evals. If you cannot measure task success, cost, latency, and failure modes, agents are just demos. I would add an eval-first step before agentic GenAI. What is the first metric you track when an agent starts drifting?

#GenAI #AIEvals #LLMEngineering

comments.author: Sönke Venjacob ⭐️
comments.comment:
You can have Claude read the room before you make a move.

One instruction—"change nothing, show me first"—turns an AI from an actor into a perfect analyst. It pulls the data, flags the issues, and drafts the narrative, but leaves the final call to you.

Where else does that "analyze, don't act" prompt prevent costly automation mistakes?

comments.author: Fabian Jaeckert
comments.comment: Harnesses make the real token bill visible; I have watched the same task swing from cents to euros once context length and retries are counted. The hidden cost is not the model price, it is the agent loop: tool errors, reruns, and long transcripts. Have you measured how much of Mistral's 10 ct result came from fewer retries versus cheaper tokens? #AgenticAI #LLMOps #AI

comments.author: Loïc Vanderschooten
comments.comment: Your system proves agents work best as critics, not cheerleaders. The hard part is making them track drift in your own rubric across years of notes, not just fetch reviews that match your mood. How do you keep them from overfitting to your past ratings? #AgenticAI #LLMEvals

comments.author: CraftOS
comments.comment:
The real problem is not letting agents create apps; it is giving them durable state, permission boundaries, and rollback when a task spans chat, files, and tools. Do you treat each Agent App like a versioned service with its own eval suite, or more like a living document?

#AgenticAI #LLMOps #RAG
